===Etymology===
From {{der|en|frm|plateforme||a [[flat]] [[form]]}}, from {{m|frm|plate||flat}} (from {{der|en|fro|plat}}, from {{der|en|grc|πλατύς||flat}}) + {{m|frm|forme||form}} (from {{der|en|la|forma|fōrma|[[shape]]; [[figure]]; form}}); compare {{m|en|flatscape}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈplætfɔːm/|/ˈplɑtfɔːm/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈplætfɔɹm/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-platform.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-GB-platform.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{rhymes|en|ætfɔː(ɹ)m|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|plat|form}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L12173}}
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q3093009}}A raised [[stage]] from which [[speech]]es are made and on which musical and other [[performance]]s are made.
#: {{syn|en|dais|podium|q2=speeches}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1915|title=Acres of Diamonds|author=Russell H. Conwell; Robert Shackleton|chapter=IV|section=His Life and Achievements|url=https://www.gutenberg.org/files/368/368-h/368-h.htm|passage=Always, whether in the pulpit or on the '''platform''', as in private conversation, there is an absolute simplicity about the man and his words; a simplicity, an earnestness, a complete honesty.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=13|passage=“{{...}} They talk of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably.” And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his '''platform''' utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes.}}
# {{senseid|en|work}} A raised floor for any purpose, e.g. for workmen during construction, or formerly for military cannon.
#: {{hypo|en|oil platform|work platform}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} A place or an opportunity to express one's opinion.
#: {{syn|en|tribune}}
#: {{ux|en|This new talk show will give a '''platform''' to everyday men and women.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Scott Cacciola|title=LeBron James said he was vaccinated, after previously evading the question.|date=2021-09-28|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/28/sports/basketball/lebron-james-covid-vaccine.html|passage=[LeBron] James did not say which vaccine he had taken or the number of doses he had received. He also said that he would not use his '''platform''' to publicly encourage others to be vaccinated.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260203201805/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/28/sports/basketball/lebron-james-covid-vaccine.html|archivedate=3 February 2026}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} Something that allows an enterprise to advance.
#: {{syn|en|foundation|stage}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 7, 2012|author=Phil McNulty|title=Moldova 0-5 England|work=BBC Sport|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19460608|passage={{w|Roy Hodgson|Hidgson}} may actually feel England could have scored even more but this was the perfect first step on the road to Rio in 2014 and the ideal '''platform''' for the second qualifier against Ukraine at {{w|Wembley Stadium|Wembley}} on Tuesday.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112083735/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19460608|archivedate=12 January 2016}}
# {{lb|en|politics|figurative}} A political [[stance]] on a broad set of issues, which are called [[plank]]s.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1652|author=w:Gerrard Winstanley|title=The Law of Freedom in a Platform|chapterurl={{fullurl:s:en:The Law of Freedom in a Platform/Chapter_1}}|chapter=1|passage=Now if the earth could be enjoyed in such a manner as every one might have provision, as it may by this '''platform''' I have offered, then will the peace of the commonwealth be preserved, and men need not act so hypocritically as the clergy do, and others likewise, to get a living.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Mike Gravel|title=Citizen Power: A People's Platform|year=1972|publisher=Holt, Rinehart and Winston|location=New York|page=xii|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/citizenpowerpeop0000grav/page/n15/mode/1up|isbn=978-0-03-091465-2|passage=Surely there is nothing strange or new or threatening about such a '''platform'''. It will distress only those who have the essentially un-American view that change itself is frightening and should be avoided at all costs.}}
# {{senseid|en|transport}} {{lb|en|transport}} A raised [[structure]] or other area alongside [[rail]]s or a [[driveway]] alongside which vehicles stop to take in and discharge [[passenger]]s.
#: {{hypo|en|island platform}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=We expressed our readiness, and in ten minutes were in the station wagon, rolling rapidly down the long drive, for it was then after nine.{{...}}As we reached the lodge we heard the whistle, and we backed up against one side of the '''platform''' as the train pulled up at the other.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=1997|title=Tryin' to Get to Heaven|author=w:Bob Dylan|album={{w|Time Out of Mind (Bob Dylan album)|Time Out of Mind}}|passage=People on the '''platforms''' / Waiting for the trains / I can hear their hearts a-beatin’ / Like pendulums swinging on chains}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=Ideas coming down the track|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838|page=13 (Technology Quarterly)|url=http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly
|passage=A “moving '''platform'''” scheme{{...}}is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails. {{...}} Stopping high-speed trains wastes energy and time, so why not simply slow them down enough for a moving '''platform''' to pull alongside?|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180223172052/https://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly|archivedate=23 February 2018}}
# {{senseid|en|track number}} {{lb|en|transport}} A specific stopping place on one of multiple tracks at a [[station]], [[numbered]] or otherwise [[named]].
#: {{synonyms|en|track}}
#* {{RQ:Rowling Harry Potter|book=1|passage=“Well, there you are, boy. '''Platform''' nine — '''platform''' ten. Your '''platform''' should be somewhere in the middle, but they don’t seem to have built it yet, do they?”}}
# {{senseid|en|Q582151}}{{lb|en|footwear|in the plural}} {{ellipsis of|en|platform shoe|t=a kind of high [[shoe]] with an extra layer between the inner and outer soles}}.
# {{lb|en|Internet}} A software system used to provide online services to clients, such as [[social media]], [[e-commerce]], or [[cloud computing]].
#: {{hypo|en|container platform|microservices platform}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838|page=71|title=End of the peer show|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21578670-peer-peer-lending-needs-new-name-end-peer-show |passage=Finance is seldom romantic. But the idea of peer-to-peer lending comes close. This is an industry that brings together individual savers and lenders on online '''platforms'''. Those that want to borrow are matched with those that want to lend.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103143947/https://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21578670-peer-peer-lending-needs-new-name-end-peer-show|archivedate=3 January 2018}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Reeves Wiedeman|title=Why Does Every Company Now Want to Be a Platform?|date=2021-09-15|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/15/books/review/jonathan-knee-platform-delusion.html|passage=The promise of the '''platform''' business model is its magical self-reinforcement: Once the '''platform''' is in place, money is supposed to flow through the system without much extra effort at all.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20241231224040/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/15/books/review/jonathan-knee-platform-delusion.html|archivedate=31 December 2024}}
# {{senseid|en|Q241317}}{{lb|en|computing}} A particular [[operating system]] or [[environment]] such as a [[database]] or other specific [[software]]; a particular type of [[computer]] or [[microprocessor]], used for running other software.
#: {{ux|en|That program runs on the X Window System '''platform'''.}}
# {{lb|en|automotive}} {{ellipsis of|en|car platform|t=a set of [[component]]s [[share]]d by several [[vehicle]] models}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Vinod K. Jain|title=Global Strategy: Competing in the Connected Economy|year=2017|publisher=Routledge|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=wqquDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA131&dq=%22car+platform%22+component&hl=&cd=3&source=gbs_api#v=onepage&q=%22car%20platform%22%20component&f=false|isbn=978-1-317-54930-7|page=131|passage=A car '''platform''' consists of the underbody, suspension, and axles, plus components such as the steering mechanism, engine, and powertrain. Using such a '''platform''', a car company can design several distinct car models to suit different customer groups{{...}}}}
# {{senseid|en|geology}} {{lb|en|geology}} A flat [[expanse]] of [[rock]], often the result of [[wave]] [[erosion]].
# {{lb|en|nautical}} A light [[deck]], usually placed in a section of the [[hold]] or over the floor of the [[magazine]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[plan]]; a [[sketch]]; a [[model]]; a [[pattern]].
#* {{RQ:Holinshed Chronicles|passage=His destruction intended by queene Quendred, hir '''platforme''' of the practise to kill him.}}
# {{lb|en|Myanmar}} A [[sidewalk]].

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L309167}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To furnish with or [[shape]] into a [[#Noun|platform]]
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1885|author=Frances Elliot|title=The Diary of an Idle Woman in Sicily| url=http://books.google.com/books?id=2W0DAAAAQAAJ|page=192| passage={{...}} upon a smiling knoll '''platformed''' by Nature {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To place on, or as if on, a platform.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1844|author=w:Elizabeth Barrett Browning|title=To Flush, My Dog
|passage=And this dog was satisfied / If a pale thin hand would glide / Down his dewlaps sloping / Which he pushed his nose within, / After—'''platforming''' his chin / On the palm left open.}}
# {{lb|en|rail}} To place a train alongside a station platform.
# {{lb|en|politics|transitive}} To include in a political platform
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[publish]] or make visible; to provide a platform for (a topic etc.).
#: {{antonyms|en|deplatform|no-platform}}
#* {{RQ:Atlantic|title=Purity Politics Makes Nothing Happen |author=Conor Friedersdorf |date=29 July 2020 |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2020/07/praise-impure-alliances/614695/ |text=If Buckley were still alive today, could a university get away with '''platforming''' him in a debate?|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251105103740/https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2020/07/praise-impure-alliances/614695/|archivedate=5 November 2025}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Andrew Lawrence|title=It platformed an alleged fraudster. Can hip-hop’s biggest radio show survive the fallout?|date=2023-12-17|url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/dec/17/breakfast-club-radio-show-alleged-ponzi-scheme-dj-envy-cesar-pina-hip-hop|passage=Half of the lawsuits against Pina also named Envy (real name: Raashaun Casey), blaming the DJ for '''platforming''' Pina on The Breakfast Club and social media.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013141642/https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/dec/17/breakfast-club-radio-show-alleged-ponzi-scheme-dj-envy-cesar-pina-hip-hop|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
#* {{RQ:New Yorker|author=w:Andrew Marantz|quotee=w:Tommy Vietor|title=The Battle for the Bros|date=2025-03-17|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2025/03/24/the-battle-for-the-bros|passage= “The ‘how dare you '''platform''' someone you disagree with’ era is over. Fuck that.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260913105127/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2025/03/24/the-battle-for-the-bros|archivedate=13 September 2026}}
# {{lb|en|film|transitive}} To open (a film) in a small number of theaters before a broader release in order to generate enthusiasm.
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Aljean Harmetz |title=Comes Fall, a Chance for Serious Movies? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/09/02/movies/comes-fall-chance-for-serious-movies.html |date=September 2, 1981 |page=C21 |text=But serious movies are not necessarily good movies. A studio that decides to '''platform''' a film had better be sure the film will get the necessary good reviews and audience approval. Otherwise, like United Artists' "A Small Circle of Friends," which was '''platformed''' around the same time as "The Elephant Man," the film will fail calamitously.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203183328/https://www.nytimes.com/1981/09/02/movies/comes-fall-chance-for-serious-movies.html|archivedate=3 December 2023}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Bernard Weinraub |title=For Movie Industry, Thanksgiving Means A Box-Office Feast |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/11/25/movies/for-movie-industry-thanksgiving-means-a-box-office-feast.html |date=November 25, 1993 |page=C11 |text=Each of these films will be "'''platformed'''," the industry term to describe the strategy of opening a movie first in a limited number of theaters to give it an aura of exclusivity, then having its appeal build through word of mouth.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250912083106/https://www.nytimes.com/1993/11/25/movies/for-movie-industry-thanksgiving-means-a-box-office-feast.html|archivedate=12 September 2025}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To form a [[plan]] of; to [[model]]; to [[lay out]].
#* {{RQ:Milton Collected Works|Reason|202|I have ſaid what is meet to ſome who do not think it for the eaſe of their inconſequent Opinions, to grant that Church-Diſcipline is '''platform'd''' in the Bible, but that it is left to the diſcretion of Men.}}
